question: A health worker is conducting an IMNCI assessment of a 3-week-old infant who was brought to the sub-centre because 'the baby is not feeding well.' The assessment reveals: axillary temperature 38.4°C, respiratory rate 68/min, umbilical redness extending to the abdominal wall, and the baby is not able to breastfeed. Which classification best describes the PRIMARY finding requiring urgent referral?

answers.text: Possible Serious Bacterial Infection (PSBI) — Pink classification, refer urgently.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. 'Not able to breastfeed' is a PSBI danger sign, as is the elevated respiratory rate (≥60/min in <2 months = fast breathing), fever, and periumbilical redness with extension. Multiple PSBI criteria are met — this is a Pink classification mandating immediate referral.

answers.text: Local Bacterial Infection — Yellow classification, treat with oral antibiotics at home.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Local bacterial infection (skin pustules, umbilical redness without extension) warrants Yellow. Here, the redness has extended to the abdominal wall — this elevates the classification. Additionally, fast breathing and inability to feed are PSBI signs, not just local infection.

answers.text: Feeding Problem — Yellow classification, counsel on breastfeeding technique and review in 2 days.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A young infant who 'is not able to breastfeed' in IMNCI is classified as a PSBI sign — this is a danger sign, NOT a simple feeding problem. The presence of fever, fast breathing, and extended periumbilical redness confirm systemic illness.

answers.text: Jaundice — Yellow classification, assess for duration and advise sun exposure.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Jaundice is a separate IMNCI domain not described here. The primary problem is a constellation of PSBI signs. Always assess all IMNCI domains and classify the most severe finding as the driving classification.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the PSBI (Possible Serious Bacterial Infection) classification criteria for the young infant. 'Not able to breastfeed' and fast breathing (RR ≥60/min) are both PSBI signs in the <2-month age group. Combined with fever and spreading periumbilical redness, this is clearly a Pink classification.

The IMNCI young-infant algorithm classifies across several domains simultaneously; the most severe classification drives the referral decision. PSBI signs include: not able to feed, fast breathing (≥60/min <2 mo), severe chest in-drawing, fever (≥38°C or hypothermia <35.5°C), movement only when stimulated, convulsions, and periumbilical redness with extension.
